case_name: Janardan Singh v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

23 April 2002
Cr.A. No. 620 of 1996
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  For the deaths of Ashok Singh and Dalan Singh, the appellant along with seven
facts: For the deaths of Ashok Singh and Dalan Singh, the appellant along with seven others was tried and charged for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 207, 148 read with Section 149 of the Penal Code, 1860 and Section 27 of the Arms Act.
The matter was reported to Police Station Sheosagar by Madan Prasad Singh, PW 8 on the same day at about 8.40 a.m.
According to the prosecution the occurrence took place on 12-11-1984 at about 6.30 a.m. in Village Auwan, District Sasaram, State of Bihar.
The informant along with his relatives requested Kedar Singh to let irrigation continue.
When Ashok Singh tried to move solely towards north and Mukhia Dalan Singh sat down in the paddy field, Janardan Singh, the appellant intimated others that Ashok is trying to escape.

After hearing noise many persons reached the spot. It was alleged that all the accused persons named in the first information report were firing and thus actually participated in the commission of the crime.
Accused Kedar Singh asked the other accused to ascertain whether Dalan Singh had actually died or not.
The prosecution had cited PW 2 Narendra Kumar Singh, PW 3 Mahendra Singh, PW 4 Bimla Devi, PW 6 Munna Singh, PW 7 Yadubansh Singh and PW 8 Madan Prasad Singh as eyewitnesses of the occurrence.
issues: Whether the appellant alone is responsible for the deaths of Ashok Singh and Dalan Singh.
Whether the High Court was correct in disbelieving the testimony of the prosecution witnesses regarding the involvement of the accused persons except the appellant.
petitioner_arguments: It would not be safe to convict and sentence the appellant on the testimony of the aforesaid eyewitnesses because the said witnesses have not been relied upon by the High Court in material particulars.
court_reasoning: The High Court has only found that the eyewitnesses have tried to implicate some of the people in the commission of the crime, who upon analysis of evidence were found to be not involved in the transaction.

A duty is cast upon the court to sift the evidence and after a close scrutiny with proper care and caution, to come to a judicial conclusion as to who out of the accused persons can be considered to have actually committed the offence.
holding: The appeal is accordingly dismissed. The bail bonds furnished by the accused are cancelled and he is directed to be taken into custody for undergoing rest of the sentence, if any. Appeal dismissed.
